quiz.title: Continuity Quiz (NCERT Ex 5.1)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on continuity at a point, discontinuities, and finding k for continuity. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Continuity and Differentiability, Exercise 5.1

questions.q: A function f is continuous at x = a when which condition holds?
options: f is defined on both sides of a
questions.explanation: Continuity at a needs three things together: f(a) is defined, lim(x→a) f(x) exists, and that limit equals f(a). Only the third option captures the full condition.

questions.q: Every polynomial function, such as f(x) = 2x³ − x + 5, is continuous at which points?
questions.explanation: Polynomials are continuous for all real x. For any point a, the limit equals the direct substitution value f(a), so no point ever fails.

questions.q: For f(x) = 1/(x − 3), at which point is the function discontinuous?
questions.explanation: A rational function is continuous wherever the denominator is non-zero. At x = 3 the denominator is 0 and f is undefined, so that is the only point of discontinuity.

questions.q: The function f(x) = |x| is continuous at x = 0 because…
questions.explanation: As x → 0 from either side, |x| → 0, and f(0) = 0. The limit equals the value, so the modulus function is continuous at 0 (it only lacks differentiability there).

questions.q: If f(x) = kx² for x ≤ 2 and f(x) = 3 for x > 2 is continuous at x = 2, then k equals:
questions.explanation: For continuity at 2 the two pieces must agree: k(2)² = 3, so 4k = 3 and k = 3/4.

questions.q: A function has a jump discontinuity at x = a when:
options: The left and right limits exist but differ
questions.explanation: A jump (or step) discontinuity occurs when both one-sided limits exist finitely but are unequal, so no single limit value can match f(a).

questions.q: For f(x) = (x² − 4)/(x − 2) with x ≠ 2, what value of f(2) makes f continuous at x = 2?
questions.explanation: For x ≠ 2, (x² − 4)/(x − 2) = x + 2, whose limit as x → 2 is 4. Defining f(2) = 4 removes the discontinuity.

questions.q: If f and g are both continuous at x = a, which of the following is guaranteed continuous at a?
questions.explanation: Sums, differences and products of continuous functions are continuous. The quotient f/g is continuous only where g(a) ≠ 0, so f + g is the safe choice.

faq.q: What is the main idea of NCERT Class 12 Exercise 5.1?
faq.a: Exercise 5.1 is entirely about continuity. You check whether a function is continuous at a given point, find every point of discontinuity, and determine the value of a constant (often k) that makes a piecewise function continuous.

faq.q: How do I check if a function is continuous at a point?
faq.a: Confirm three things at that point: f(a) is defined, the limit as x approaches a exists (left-hand limit equals right-hand limit), and that limit equals f(a). If all three hold, f is continuous there.

faq.q: Which functions are continuous everywhere in this exercise?
faq.a: Every polynomial is continuous for all real x. Rational functions are continuous wherever the denominator is non-zero, and the modulus function |x| is continuous everywhere, including at x = 0.

faq.q: How do you find the value of k for continuity?
faq.a: Set the two pieces of the function equal at the breakpoint. Compute the left-hand and right-hand limits there, equate them to f at that point, and solve the resulting equation for k.
